title: Voice (sustained sung vowels)
reference_instrument: adult male voice, sustained vowels (VocalSet long tones, CC BY 4.0)
summary: A lumped two-mass vocal-fold model phonates into a 44-section MRI-derived vocal tract and the radiated pressure is read at a baffled microphone. The oscillation is not imposed: it emerges from the fold, Bernoulli aperture, fold collision and tract loop. The tract comes from one male speaker's MRI area functions in a speech posture (Story 2008). The first renders are exploratory fixtures; nothing is claimed about their match to a singer until the grader has compared them with real recordings.
physics_present: Two-mass fold (Ishizaka-Flanagan masses and stiffnesses from the licensed model-card pack) as a port-Hamiltonian system with a Bernoulli aperture and fold collision, self-oscillating against the tract (fs-couple glottis.rs, fs-phs, fs-dcontact).

Vocal tract as a 44-section area function from Story (2008) Table I, with viscothermal loss and a flanged-piston radiation load from the transfer-matrix duct (fs-duct), played through a convergence-laddered characteristic line.

Mouth volume flow from the SAME transfer-matrix duct (driving_point::outlet, a laddered FIR driven by the island's incident wave), radiated through the baffled circular-opening receiver at the paper's recording geometry: 0.30 m, 45 degrees off axis.
Output is the retarded derivative of the physical mouth flow at the microphone; the supraglottal pressure is never the output and no source waveform, formant filter or gain is applied.
physics_missing: Tract wall: the primary descriptions use rigid walls. The yielding-wall impedance is UNKNOWN here (it would come from direct vocal-tract wall-impedance measurements), and the paper's own calculation included yielding walls, so formant widths and low-frequency damping differ by that gap. Two variants carry an authored, uncited wall estimate, to measure the wall's effect on /a/ (the /u/ one is refused like the rigid /u/, see below).

Numerical: the tract lines are FIRs capped at 65536 taps, 0.68 s at the 96 kHz physical clock. The lightly damped lip-constriction resonances of /u/ ring past that, so /u/ is refused at 96 kHz with or without the wall estimate (ladder tail 1.08e-10 rigid, 6.07e-8 with the estimate, against 1e-10) and is rendered at a 48 kHz physical clock, where the same cap spans 1.37 s. That puts /u/ on a different mechanics rate from the other vowels; a pole-extracted line for long-ringing tracts is the missing piece.
Singing posture: the area functions are the speech configuration of the MRI subject, lying supine. Larynx height, pharynx and lip shape differ in singing, and no sung-posture MRI is entered.
Radiation: an infinite baffle replaces the head and torso, so there is no head diffraction. Nasal coupling, the piriform sinuses and other side cavities are not in the series plane-wave tract.

Fold tissue: a lumped two-mass card, not layered body-cover tissue or a 3D fold. The damping ratio and the collision law are authored estimates. Pitch is set by one stiffness factor per description, found by iterating the emergent f0 of the model alone to the target note (within 3 cents, no recording involved), so f0 matches by construction and is not evidence of fidelity. The factor differs between vowels at the same note (0.63 to 0.75 of the pack values at D#3) because the tract loads the fold; a physical fold-elongation law would replace this one free scale.

Subglottal system and player: the subglottal pressure is an authored player input (900 Pa times the stiffness factor), not a measured one, and there is no lung or trachea coupling. Vibrato, register changes and formant-tuning gestures are absent.
Grading: no comparison with VocalSet recordings has been made yet, so no statement about timbre, formant frequencies or onset behaviour against real singers is supported.
